title: Keep internal service ports private

verify.summary: Fresh independent verification passed source bindings and confirmed only loopback HTTPS edge publication, but the bounded runtime scan finds a pre-existing host PostgreSQL listener on 127.0.0.1:5432 and no distinct external observer is available. Source-only evidence cannot satisfy FT-003-AC-019.

The real-runtime topology proof is deferred until the application is actually running in the real runtime; before that point this verification is optional and is not a blocker for local feature implementation. Keep the task-specific acceptance evidence pending. Later, run /exe TASK-065-T3-FT-003-W1 on an isolated pilot-host-capable environment with an authorized outside observer; do not publish internal ports or mutate native PostgreSQL as an inferred task tactic.

Source bindings and local topology checks are accepted for current Linux development. External observer/private-port evidence is deferred until the real server exists and is not a current queue gateway.
verify.resume_route: when the real server exists, run the already-defined external private-port scan as follow-up acceptance evidence

evidence_required: FT-003-AC-019 RED: no focused source/runtime proof limits externally reachable ports; GREEN: source-managed Compose/edge bindings and an external scan show only the pilot HTTPS edge reachable while PostgreSQL, MinIO and backend/worker/realtime internal ports remain private and the client flow publishes none; decisive comparison: scripts/check-private-topology.sh reconciles declared bindings, listening sockets and external scan targets without printing credentials; artifact: redacted topology report under .tasks/TASK-065-T3-FT-003-W1/.
purpose: Own the independently deployable private-port topology control.
success_outcome: Only the intended HTTPS edge is externally reachable; every internal role/data service stays private.
anti_goals: Do not change application routes, browser policies or SSH authentication.
Do not publish PostgreSQL/MinIO/internal role ports for testing.
Do not add firewall orchestration beyond the source-managed pilot topology.

forbidden_scope: LNA/SSH/browser controls owned by TASK-063, TASK-064 and TASK-049
stop_conditions: Privacy cannot be proved without exposing an internal port.
Fix requires a production network redesign.
Inspection would disclose protected connection data.

constraints: Use source-managed bind/publish configuration and a read-only external scan.
Scan only the intended pilot host/ports and redact sensitive connection data.
Keep the HTTPS edge behavior unchanged.
invariants: Only HTTPS edge is externally reachable.
PostgreSQL, MinIO and internal application-role ports remain private.
Client flow creates no port exposure.
verification_targets: Negative external reachability for every internal service.
Review confirms no testing-only port publication remains.
